summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 4, part 143) set during a city siege. Ana confronts soldiers arriving at her home, and Valentine, a figure with hearing aids, turns the tables on a captured wizard by secretly recording him. The narrative then jumps forward: after the wizard's arrest, robots and sky-cars crush the enemy, services and buildings are restored, and the siege ends fourteen days later. Valentine and Trover bury their mother in a robot-dug grave marked HERO OF THE SIEGE.
one_line: In a besieged city, Valentine records a captured wizard, and the siege ends two weeks later as Valentine and Trover bury their mother.
key_facts: Ana sees a line of soldiers in the road carrying weapons ranging from knives to old gunpowder weapons to small, floppy sidearms.
Ana says, "I knew it would be today," after Valentine came back that morning.
The old hero tells Ana to call them out because "They already know you're here."
The wizard says "It's all gone" and "You won't get a scrap of it."
The general says to the wizard, "You were very well-fed."
Valentine reveals she is recording the wizard through her hearing aids and asks if he has any words for the microphone.
The wizard's body crumples in the grasp of the soldier who holds him after Valentine's recording reveal.
Three days after the wizard's arrest, the sky-cars lift off again and drop intelligent motes that burrow into enemy soldiers' heads.
Four days after the wizard's arrest, the printers start to supply food and drugs.
Ten days after the wizard's arrest, the buildings start to repair themselves and the lifts all work again.
Fourteen days after the wizard's arrest, the siege ends.
Valentine and Trover bury their mother that morning in a perfectly square grave in the woods, dug by robots.
Each grave is marked with a small plaque bearing a name, a date of birth, sometimes a day of death, and the legend HERO OF THE SIEGE.
Trover tosses in the first shovel-full of dirt at their mother's grave and does not speak all day.
